heading.en: How much food does a field make?

hook.en: Every gram of rice, grass or wood starts as sunlight captured by a leaf. Ecologists measure how fast plants turn that light into new organic matter.
hook.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ಗ್ರಾಂ ಅಕ್ಕಿ, ಹುಲ್ಲು ಅಥವಾ ಮರ ಎಲೆಯು ಹಿಡಿದ ಸೂರ್ಯನ ಬೆಳಕಿನಿಂದಲೇ ಆರಂಭವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಸಸ್ಯಗಳು ಆ ಬೆಳಕನ್ನು ಎಷ್ಟು ವೇಗವಾಗಿ ಹೊಸ ಸಾವಯವ ವಸ್ತುವಾಗಿಸುತ್ತವೆ ಎಂದು ಪರಿಸರ ವಿಜ್ಞಾನಿಗಳು ಅಳೆಯುತ್ತಾರೆ.

objectives.en: Distinguish GPP, NPP and secondary productivity
Compare the productivity of oceans and land

narration.en: Every gram of rice, grass or wood starts as sunlight captured by a leaf. Ecologists measure how fast plants turn that light into new organic matter.
narration.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ಗ್ರಾಂ ಅಕ್ಕಿ, ಹುಲ್ಲು ಅಥವಾ ಮರ ಎಲೆಯು ಹಿಡಿದ ಸೂರ್ಯನ ಬೆಳಕಿನಿಂದಲೇ ಆರಂಭವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಸಸ್ಯಗಳು ಆ ಬೆಳಕನ್ನು ಎಷ್ಟು ವೇಗವಾಗಿ ಹೊಸ ಸಾವಯವ ವಸ್ತುವಾಗಿಸುತ್ತವೆ ಎಂದು ಪರಿಸರ ವಿಜ್ಞಾನಿಗಳು ಅಳೆಯುತ್ತಾರೆ.

body.en: A constant input of solar energy is the basic requirement for any ecosystem to function and sustain. Primary production is the amount of biomass or organic matter produced per unit area over a time period by plants during photosynthesis. It is expressed in terms of weight (g m$^{-2}$) or energy (kcal m$^{-2}$). The rate of biomass production is called productivity, expressed in g m$^{-2}$ yr$^{-1}$ or (kcal m$^{-2}$) yr$^{-1}$, to compare the productivity of different ecosystems. Gross primary productivity (GPP) is the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis. A considerable amount of GPP is used by plants in respiration (R). Gross primary productivity minus respiration losses is the net primary productivity (NPP). NPP is the biomass available for the consumption of heterotrophs (herbivores and decomposers). Secondary productivity is the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers.

points.en: Productivity units: g m⁻² yr⁻¹ or kcal m⁻² yr⁻¹
GPP: rate of organic matter made in photosynthesis
NPP = GPP − R: available to herbivores and decomposers
Secondary productivity: new organic matter made by consumers

narration.en: Gross primary productivity is the rate at which plants make organic matter by photosynthesis. Subtract what the plants use in respiration and you get net primary productivity, the food available to herbivores and decomposers.
narration.kn: ಒಟ್ಟು ಪ್ರಾಥಮಿಕ ಉತ್ಪಾದಕತೆ ಎಂದರೆ ದ್ಯುತಿಸಂಶ್ಲೇಷಣೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಸಸ್ಯಗಳು ಸಾವಯವ ವಸ್ತು ತಯಾರಿಸುವ ದರ. ಉಸಿರಾಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಬಳಸಿದ್ದನ್ನು ಕಳೆದರೆ ನಿವ್ವಳ ಪ್ರಾಥಮಿಕ ಉತ್ಪಾದಕತೆ ಸಿಗುತ್ತದೆ; ಇದು ಸಸ್ಯಾಹಾರಿಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ವಿಘಟಕಗಳಿಗೆ ಲಭ್ಯ ಆಹಾರ.

say.en: Gross primary productivity, GPP, is the rate at which plants make organic matter in photosynthesis. Part of it is used up by the plants in respiration.
What remains is net primary productivity, NPP. It is the food available to herbivores and decomposers.
So NPP equals GPP minus R. Productivity is measured in grams or kilocalories per square metre per year.

text.en: g m⁻² yr⁻¹ or kcal m⁻² yr⁻¹

say.en: Worked example: GPP 2400 and respiration 900 kilocalories per square metre per year. NPP is 1500, which is 62.5 per cent of GPP.
The whole biosphere makes about 170 billion tons of NPP a year, dry weight. Oceans cover about 70 per cent of the surface but make only 55 billion tons.

What remains is net primary productivity, NPP. It is the food available to herbivores and decomposers. So NPP equals GPP minus R. NPP is 1500, which is 62.5 per cent of GPP. The whole biosphere makes about 170 billion tons of NPP a year, dry weight. Oceans cover about 70 per cent of the surface but make only 55 billion tons.
Follow 1000 units of sunlight down to the food a herbivore can use. Change how much PAR plants capture and how much they burn in respiration.

caption.en: Less than half of sunlight is PAR, and plants capture only 2–10 per cent of the PAR as GPP. Respiration uses part of the GPP; what is left is the NPP, available to herbivores and decomposers. Consumers turn a small part of what they eat into new biomass: secondary productivity.
caption.kn: ಸೂರ್ಯಬೆಳಕಿನ ಅರ್ಧಕ್ಕಿಂತ ಕಡಿಮೆ PAR; ಸಸ್ಯಗಳು PAR ನ 2–10% ಮಾತ್ರ GPP ಆಗಿ ಹಿಡಿಯುತ್ತವೆ. ಉಸಿರಾಟದ ನಂತರ ಉಳಿದದ್ದು NPP. ಭಕ್ಷಕರು ಅದರ ಸಣ್ಣ ಭಾಗವನ್ನು ಹೊಸ ಜೀವರಾಶಿಯಾಗಿಸುತ್ತಾರೆ.

body.en: Primary productivity depends on the plant species inhabiting a particular area. It also depends on a variety of environmental factors, the availability of nutrients and the photosynthetic capacity of plants, so it varies across ecosystems. The annual net primary productivity of the whole biosphere is approximately 170 billion tons (dry weight) of organic matter. Despite occupying about 70 per cent of the surface, the productivity of the oceans is only 55 billion tons; the rest is on land.

points.en: Depends on species, environment, nutrients, photosynthetic capacity
Biosphere NPP ≈ 170 billion tons (dry weight) per year
Oceans: ~70% of surface but only 55 billion tons

narration.en: Productivity depends on the plant species, the environment, nutrients and photosynthetic capacity. The whole biosphere makes about 170 billion tons of organic matter a year, and the oceans, though they cover about 70 per cent of the surface, make only 55 billion tons of it.
narration.kn: ಉತ್ಪಾದಕತೆ ಸಸ್ಯ ಪ್ರಭೇದ, ಪರಿಸರ, ಪೋಷಕಾಂಶ ಮತ್ತು ದ್ಯುತಿಸಂಶ್ಲೇಷಣಾ ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯವನ್ನು ಅವಲಂಬಿಸಿದೆ. ಇಡೀ ಜೀವಗೋಳ ವರ್ಷಕ್ಕೆ ಸುಮಾರು 170 ಬಿಲಿಯನ್ ಟನ್ ಸಾವಯವ ವಸ್ತು ತಯಾರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ; ಸುಮಾರು 70% ಮೇಲ್ಮೈ ಆವರಿಸಿದ ಸಾಗರಗಳ ಪಾಲು ಕೇವಲ 55 ಬಿಲಿಯನ್ ಟನ್.

problem.en: A grassland has a GPP of 2,400 kcal m⁻² yr⁻¹. The grasses use 900 kcal m⁻² yr⁻¹ in respiration. Find the NPP and the fraction of GPP available to herbivores and decomposers.

steps.en: NPP = GPP − R = 2,400 − 900 = 1,500 kcal m⁻² yr⁻¹.

answer.en: NPP = 1,500 kcal m⁻² yr⁻¹, i.e. 62.5% of GPP.

problem.en: Of the biosphere's annual NPP of about 170 billion tons, oceans contribute 55 billion tons. What percentage comes from land?

answer.en: About 68% comes from land, though land is only about 30% of the surface.
